method: Compared with the pdftotext text layer (raw and -layout modes) of the official PDF (SHA-256 checked) and its official marking scheme. No PDF-to-image renderer was available in this environment, so visual inspection of the page images was not possible; findings for the pervasive math-font glyph loss rely on the text layer, the marking scheme's arithmetic, and independent re-derivation of each answer.

source.notes: QP sha256 matches source.sha256 exactly. sourceUrl/answerSourceUrl are both on cbse.gov.in. Document header confirms MATHEMATICS (STANDARD), Q.P. Code 30/1/1, Series GE1FH, SET~1, 27 printed pages, 38 questions, Maximum Marks 80, Time 3 hours — all matching the pack's source metadata. Confirms the pack's own note: this PDF's text layer has severe, systemic loss of Greek letters, minus signs, root signs, degree signs and stacked fractions/powers (embedded math font glyph-to-Unicode mapping issue), affecting both the question paper and (to a lesser extent) the marking scheme.

questions.reason: α, β and the entire relation connecting them are missing from the stem (page 3); options (B) and (D) are missing minus signs and duplicate (A) and (C); the marking scheme's own answer text '(D) 4' is also missing a minus sign.

Minus signs before '3y' and 'b' are missing from both equations in the stem (page 5); verified x=1, y=2, a=4, b=8 satisfies 2a=b, so the equations as reconstructed (2x−3y+a=0, 2x+3y−b=0) and the answer are consistent, but the printed stem itself is missing the signs.
questions.notes: Independently verified: with the reconstructed equations, a=4 and b=8, giving 2a=b, matching option (B).

questions.reason: Minus sign in point P's x-coordinate is missing on page 5 (stored as 'P( 4, 5)', likely 'P(−4, 5)').

θ is missing throughout the stem and degree signs are missing from all options (page 5); the marking scheme's own answer text reads '(B) 300', which the source notes flag as a likely corrupted '30°' (a lost degree glyph silently merged with the digit).
θ is missing after 'tan²' in the stem; option (C) is missing its minus sign and duplicates option (A) ('1' instead of '−1'), page 5.
The operator between 'n' and '7 m' is missing from the stem (page 5), likely 'n − 7m'.

questions.notes: Stem and all four options match the QP text layer exactly (page 7, verified in both raw and -layout modes); no notation needed; officialAnswer (A) parallel matches the marking scheme exactly.

The graph of the two polynomials (page 7) is not reproduced; the number of distinct zeroes cannot be counted from text alone.

Stem and options are plain text, no math notation involved; matches QP text layer exactly (page 9).

The second bound of the interval is missing from the stem ('...a rational number between 3 and ?', page 9); options (B) and (C), irrational/root values, are also blank.
Degree sign after '72' is missing from the stem; option (D) is missing its square-root sign in the pack's stored options ('10 2 units' vs the marking scheme's clean '10√2 units'), page 11.

Figure (circle with tangent PA and points O, B) on page 11 is not reproduced and is needed to determine the configuration of B relative to A and O; angle/degree symbols are also missing from the stem.
Degree sign after '30' is missing from the stem; options (C) and (D) both read identically as '150 m' with their square-root signs lost (page 11).
The radius numeric value is missing from the stem ('an arc of a circle of radius cm', page 13); degree signs are also missing from all four options.

The Assertion's probability value reads 'is 1.' but is almost certainly a truncated fraction (likely 'is 1/20.'); the assertion-reason answer codes themselves are boilerplate and printed intact (page 13).

A π symbol is missing from the Reason's formula ('3 r²'); since the marking scheme confirms Reason (R) is false, '3' is plausibly the printed (intentionally wrong) coefficient with only π lost, but this cannot be confirmed without the image (page 13).

Degree signs are missing after all four angle values; more importantly, the marking scheme's intermediate step (x(1/2)+y(1)+1/2−1=5) contains an unexplained '−1' term not evident anywhere in the printed stem, suggesting more than cosmetic notation is missing (page 15).

The entire expression to evaluate is missing from the stem (only the word 'Evaluate :' survives, page 15); officialAnswer '(√3)²=2' is a best-effort reconstruction of a stacked-fraction working that cannot be independently confirmed.
Coefficients of p(x) are missing from the stem (stored as 'x² + x .'); the marking scheme's working implies p(x) = x² + (4/3)x − 4/3, page 15.
questions.notes: Independently verified: (1/3)(3x²+4x−4) = (1/3)(3x−2)(x+2), zeroes 2/3 and −2, matches officialAnswer and is internally consistent.

questions.notes: Stem is plain text and matches the QP exactly (page 17), no notation needed there. officialAnswer's ∠/°/Δ/²/√ symbols were silently rebuilt from a marking scheme whose own text layer also lost them; independently re-verified: OA=√(26²−10²)=√576=24, radius=24 m.

questions.notes: officialAnswer content (∠OCA=∠OAC via OA=OC, ∠OCD=90° tangent-radius, giving ∠BAC+∠ACD=90°) is a standard, internally consistent proof matching the marking scheme.

Stem matches QP exactly (page 17); this is a general proof where the student draws their own quadrilateral, so no external figure is needed. officialAnswer's ∠ symbols were rebuilt from a marking scheme whose own text layer lost them, but the proof structure (∠1=∠2, ..., 2(∠1+∠4+∠5+∠8)=360° ⇒ ∠AOB+∠COD=180°) is the standard, correct proof of this well-known result.

questions.notes: officialAnswer reconstructs the standard identity tanθ/(1−cotθ)+cotθ/(1−tanθ)=1+secθcosecθ; independently verified as a well-known, correct identity matching the marking scheme's derivation steps.

questions.reason: The trigonometric identity to be proved is missing from the stem entirely (only 'Prove that :' survives, page 19).
questions.notes: officialAnswer reconstructs sinA/(sinA−cosA)+cosA/(sinA+cosA)=2/(2sin²A−1); independently verified algebraically as correct and matching the marking scheme's derivation steps.

questions.reason: Point A is printed as (5, 6) but the marking scheme's own arithmetic (y = (−4(5)−6)/(5+1)) implies A's y-coordinate is actually −6, not 6 — a sign the pack's own extraction notes did not flag. Point B's minus signs ('( 1, 4)') are also missing, likely (−1,−4). Page 19.
questions.notes: Independently verified: with A(5,−6), B(−1,−4), section formula on the x-axis gives k=5 (ratio 5:1), matching the printed step '0=(−k+5)/(k+1) ⇒ k=5'; y=(−4(5)−6)/6=−26/6=−13/3, matching officialAnswer exactly.

questions.reason: The specific number to be proved irrational is missing from the stem ('Prove that is an irrational number.'); the marking scheme's proof structure implies it is likely '1/√5', but this is not stated in the pack's question text (page 19).

The air-volume value and the value to use for π are both missing from the stem (page 19). officialAnswer's own derivation is internally inconsistent: '1408 = (8/3)×(22/7)×r³ ⇒ r³=8' does not follow arithmetically ((8/3)(22/7)=176/21≈8.38, giving r³≈168, not 8).
questions.notes: The marking-scheme layout shows '1408' stacked directly above '21', suggesting the true volume is 1408/21 m³, not 1408 m³ as narrated in officialAnswer: 1408/21 = (8/3)(22/7) r³ ⇒ r³ = (1408/21)×(21/176) = 8, which is consistent with r=2 m. This should be corrected, not republished as narrated.

questions.reason: A leading instruction clause is missing before 'in the following table' (likely 'Find the missing frequency f...', page 21). More seriously, officialAnswer's mode value (19.95) does not follow from the printed class width: the table's classes are 11–13, 13–15, ... (width 2), but the mode formula as given uses a multiplier of 3, not 2.
questions.notes: Independently verified: mean is solid — with x_i=12,14,16,18,20,22,24 and f_i=7,6,9,13,f,5,4, ΣfiXi=752+20f and Σfi=44+f, so 18=(752+20f)/(44+f) gives f=20 regardless of width. But the mode formula L+[(f1−f0)/(2f1−f0−f2)]×h with L=19,f1=20,f0=13,f2=5,h=2 gives 19+7/22×2≈19.64, not 19.95. Using h=3 (as the marking scheme's printed working does) gives 19.95. Either the marking scheme used the wrong class width, or the true printed intervals have width 3 (e.g. 11–14, 14–17, ...) and were mis-extracted; this cannot be resolved from the text layer alone and should be checked against the PDF image before publishing.

Full case-study text matches QP exactly (page 23), including sub-question marks (1,1,2,2). Independently verified: AP 300,350,400,...; a4=450,a5=500,a6=550; a8=650; S10=5250; S6=2250 — all match officialAnswer and marking scheme.
